## TRA Timeline

#### Re-IPO and TRA execution

- 2018-03-20: S-1 files the form-of TRA as Exhibit 10.14
- 2018-04-23: Re-IPO closes; TRA executed between GrafTech International Ltd. and Brookfield Capital Partners IV GP, Ltd. on inherited pre-IPO tax assets (U.S. NOLs, Section 959 previously taxed income, foreign tax credits, Swiss NOLs)
- 2018-04-25: 8-K reports IPO close and TRA execution

#### LIBOR-to-SOFR amendment and restatement

- 2023-04-10: Amended and Restated TRA executed; interest rate updated from LIBOR plus 1.00% to one-month SOFR plus 1.10% (mechanical LIBOR-transition update only)
- 2024-02-14: A&R TRA filed as Exhibit 10.15 to the FY2023 10-K

#### Valuation-allowance write-down

- 2025-06-30: Full valuation allowance recorded against U.S. deferred tax assets; remaining $3.8M TRA liability written off to Other expense (income); contract remains legally in force

## Explanation

GrafTech's TRA originated at its April 23, 2018 re-IPO out of Brookfield ownership and is a non-Up-C sponsor-take-private-then-re-IPO TRA: rather than covering exchanges of LLC units, it monetizes pre-existing tax attributes inherited from the 2015 Brookfield take-private (U.S. NOLs, Section 959 previously taxed income, foreign tax credits, and certain Swiss subsidiary NOLs). The public company pays 85% of cash savings from utilizing those attributes to Brookfield Capital Partners IV GP, Ltd. as the sole beneficiary. The April 10, 2023 Amended and Restated TRA only updated the interest-rate index from LIBOR plus 100 bp to one-month SOFR plus 110 bp; the 2020-2021 dividend recapitalizations did not trigger a Change of Control. The recorded liability has trended down from $86.5M at origin to $5.8M at year-end 2024; in Q2 2025 GrafTech booked a full valuation allowance on its U.S. deferred tax assets and wrote off the remaining $3.8M, leaving the contract legally in force but with no recorded liability. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing record and the A&R amendment text.
